client_tls_rejected.title: The client rejected the ProxyPilot certificate
client_tls_rejected.body: The TLS handshake started, but the client closed the connection after receiving the certificate generated by ProxyPilot. No request was decrypted. After 3 rejections ProxyPilot stops decrypting this host and passes its traffic through untouched until the next restart, so the app keeps working.
causes: The ProxyPilot root CA is not installed or not trusted on this device.
The app uses SSL pinning for this host.
Android 7+: the app does not trust user-installed certificates.

client_tls_error.title: TLS handshake with the client failed
client_tls_error.body: The client and ProxyPilot could not agree on a TLS session.
causes: The client requires a TLS version or cipher the proxy does not offer.
The client sent non-TLS data on a TLS port.

upstream_tls_error.title: The server's certificate could not be verified
upstream_tls_error.body: ProxyPilot connected to the server, but the TLS handshake with it failed.
causes: The server uses a self-signed or expired certificate.
The server requires a client certificate (mTLS).

upstream_connect_error.title: Could not reach the server
upstream_connect_error.body: ProxyPilot could not open a connection to the upstream host, or it closed while sending the response.
causes: The host name does not resolve (DNS).
The server is down or the port is closed.
A firewall or VPN blocks the connection.

timeout.title: The request timed out
timeout.body: The server did not answer in time.
causes: The server is slow or overloaded.

client_aborted.title: The client cancelled the request
client_aborted.body: The client closed the connection before the response finished.
causes: The app cancelled the request (navigation, timeout, retry).
The user closed the page or app.

proxy_loop.title: Request loop detected
proxy_loop.body: The request was addressed to the proxy itself and was rejected to avoid an infinite loop.
causes: The client is configured to send its proxy traffic to ProxyPilot's own address as a target.

aborted.title: Request aborted by a rule or breakpoint
aborted.body: A rule or a breakpoint decision stopped this request.
causes: A breakpoint was resolved with Abort.

unknown.title: The request failed
unknown.body: ProxyPilot recorded an error for this flow.

mcp.title: AI agents (MCP)
mcp.body: Give Claude Code, Cursor or any MCP client direct access to your traffic: list and search requests, read bodies and WebSocket messages, mock responses, set breakpoints and throttle the network. ProxyPilot must be running (this page means it is).
mcp.claudeNote: -s user makes it available in every project. Start a new Claude Code session to load the tools.
mcp.otherNote: Add this to the client's mcpServers config. Use the full path of proxypilot if it is not on PATH. Add "--read-only" to the args to block rules and edits.
mcp.tryBody: Ask your agent: "Using proxypilot, which requests failed in the last 5 minutes and why?"

setup.iosBody: Simulators use the Mac's network settings. Install the ProxyPilot CA into each simulator, then turn on the macOS system proxy so Safari and apps send their traffic through ProxyPilot.

device.title: Physical device
device.body: Connect an iPhone or Android phone on the same Wi-Fi. Scan the code with the phone camera to open the certificate page, set the Wi-Fi proxy, and trust the certificate.
device.loopback: The proxy listens on {addr} only, so phones cannot reach it. Turn on the switch above, or restart it on all interfaces from the terminal (only on a network you trust):
device.firewall: The macOS firewall is on. If the phone cannot connect, allow incoming connections for ProxyPilot in System Settings → Network → Firewall → Options.
device.noLan: This Mac has no LAN address. Connect it to the same Wi-Fi as the phone.
iosSteps: Settings → Wi-Fi → (i) next to your network → Configure Proxy → Manual → server {ip}, port {port}.
In Safari open http://proxypilot.cert and allow the profile download.
Settings → General → About → Certificate Trust Settings → turn on full trust for the ProxyPilot CA.
androidSteps: Settings → Network → Wi-Fi → your network → Edit → Advanced → Proxy: Manual, host {ip}, port {port}.
In the browser open http://proxypilot.cert and download the .crt.
Settings → Security → Encryption & credentials → Install a certificate → CA certificate.
Apps trust user CAs only in debug builds with a network_security_config; browsers work right away.
device.noDevices: Waiting for a device… It appears here with its first request.
device.rejectedHint: {host} refused the ProxyPilot certificate: trust it on the device, or the app pins its certificate.
device.lanOff: Off: only this Mac can use the proxy. Turn it on to connect a phone on the same Wi-Fi.
device.lanOn: On: anyone on this Wi-Fi can use the proxy on port {port}. Turn it off when you're done, especially on shared networks.
device.lanFixed: On because the proxy was started with --proxy-listen {addr}. Restart without it to make this switchable.

setup.installed: Installed the CA on {name}. Restart the app to pick it up.
setup.simNote: The CA stays installed after the simulator shuts down. Restart the app after installing so it picks up the new trust.
setup.noSims: No simulators found. Create one in Xcode → Window → Devices and Simulators.
setup.sysProxyBody: Points HTTP and HTTPS of every network service at {target}. Bypass: localhost, 127.0.0.1, *.local.
setup.restoreNote: Turning it off restores the exact previous settings from a backup. `proxypilot stop` does it too.
setup.needsAdmin: macOS asked for administrator rights. Run these commands in Terminal:
setup.onThisMac: on this Mac (needed for macOS apps, not for simulators)

android.body: ProxyPilot sets the device's proxy over adb. Emulators reach this Mac at 10.0.2.2; USB devices use adb reverse, so Wi-Fi does not matter.

android.noDevices: No device. Start an emulator, or connect a phone with USB debugging on and accept the prompt.
android.unauthorized: Unlock the phone and accept the USB debugging prompt.

android.flutter: Flutter ignores the Android proxy. In debug builds:

chrome.title: Chrome
chrome.body: Capture Chrome tabs over the DevTools protocol: no proxy and no certificate. Rules (Map Local, rewrite, map remote, breakpoints) apply to these requests too.
chrome.launchHint: Opens Chrome with a separate ProxyPilot profile. Chrome does not allow debugging your main profile.
chrome.attachHint: Or connect to a Chrome you started yourself with --remote-debugging-port:
chrome.macHint: macOS may ask whether Chrome may use its keychain or accept connections for the new profile; denying is fine.
